title: The Minion Stuff I'm Most Excited For in PoE 2 1.0

sections.title: Intro
points: The Demon Magus might be the coolest thing they've done with minions so far in PoE 2.
No new minion class in 1.0 - but a LOT of minion stuff to go through.
This is everything minion-related I'm most excited for - Demon Magus first.
**Subscribe** - I'll break down the patch notes the moment they drop.
prompts: Why does Demon Magus top your list over everything else?
deeper: You'd been screaming about Demon Magus since the 0.1 datamining.
You let out a shout at the reveal before the crowd connected the dots.

sections.title: Ground rules
points: My take from the ExileCon playtest - not a guide, not a tier list.
I only properly tested Demon Magus behaviour: one spell gem plus Unearth and Bone Storm.
! No final minion numbers until the 1.0 patch notes are out.
prompts: What else minion-related did you get to see or touch at ExileCon?

sections.title: Demon Magus
points: Infernalist ascendancy: binds a Scourge Demon to you - socket multiple spells AND supports, it follows you and casts them.
Tooltip: Reviving companion - you pay its spell costs, but they cost 50% less.
+ Scaling hook: 15% more damage per **different** socketed skill - variety pays.
Playtest: it fired the cooldown spell whenever ready, otherwise spammed the main one - behaviour looked pretty good.
- Open question: does it scale past gem level 20? Couldn't get an answer.
The story: I brought it up with Jonathan and Mark on Tavern Talk - Mark said that reminded him it existed.
> If it's really good I take all the credit - if it's bad, it's all on Mark.
prompts: Which spells and supports are you socketing first?
Does it feel like a real minion or more like a totem that follows you?
Performance verdict so far - or still too early?
deeper: Similar idea on Acolyte of Chayula: Keeper of the Flame, a clone companion that uses any Quarterstaff skill you give it.
You said you don't know about its performance yet - limited gems in the playtest.

sections.title: Triple Infernal Hounds & Covenants
points: Infernal Hounds got a huge upgrade: three hounds plus a command skill to charge in and explode.
! You do NOT get all three by default - the node behind Infernal Hounds gives the two extra.
Show it in PoB: one hound without that point, three with it.
Command: Instability - one hound charges, leaps and explodes: 1632-2447 fire damage, 1.9 m radius.
Timothy and Viper told me there's definitely a build around the hounds exploding things.
Covenants: Infernal Covenant lets you pick Covenant of Beidat, Ghorr or K'Tash.
Covenant of Ghorr: drains 5% life a second, spawns Withering Bloatflies every 2 s, +15% more damage over time.
prompts: Is the exploding-hound build real or a meme?
Which Covenant are you building around - and is 5% life a second worth it?
deeper: Hound pops with a faster revive - you said that's definitely playable.
Beidat and K'Tash were only shown by name - their tooltips weren't on screen.

sections.title: Dancing Dervish
points: Dancing Dervish is coming to PoE 2.
PoE 1 version: a sword that starts Rampage - then it leaves your hands and becomes a cycloning minion.
You're unarmed while it spins around killing everything - pure minion fantasy.
I want a build around it - balance changes pending.
prompts: Which class or ascendancy would you put it on in PoE 2?
Is it a fun toy or a real build in your eyes?
deeper: You said it should be really fun - and doubted Duelist is the best home for it.

sections.title: Also on my list
points: Permanent zombies
The new staff
Arakaali's Fang
New spectres
! Details on these land with the patch notes.
prompts: Permanent zombies: what changes and what does it unlock?
The new staff: what did you see, and does it change your build plans?
Arakaali's Fang: what do you expect it to do in PoE 2?
New spectres: which one are you most excited to test?

sections.title: More minion news from the keynote
points: Siege Breaker belt: order your minions to charge at enemies and detonate.
Dominate: a curse that turns enemies into minions - they're resurrected to serve you after dying.
+ Living Lightning no longer deals minion damage - it now uses attack or spell damage.
prompts: Siege Breaker with exploding hounds - combo or overkill?
Any minion balance change you're hoping for in the patch notes?

sections.title: Final thoughts
points: Heavily leaning Infernalist - triple hellhounds and Demon Magus.
Demon Magus is most likely the first thing I play.
Everything else on the list gets a real verdict once patch notes are out.
prompts: If you had to lock in one minion build for 1.0 today, what is it?

sections.title: Outro
points: Which minion change are YOU most excited for? Comments.
1.0 launch subathon on 11 December - come hang out.
Thanks for watching - see you in 1.0.

Unearth.summary: The keynote did not show or describe any changes to Unearth itself; the word "unearthing" appeared only in flavor text about empowered boss effects and league mechanics. Its tooltip wasn't shown yet.

Acolyte of Chayula.summary: The Acolyte of Chayula has been totally reworked: Herald of Chayula now causes all your hits to add Decay to monsters, and killing a monster triggers an explosion based on the Decay it had. The old Darkness mechanic has been moved entirely into a keystone on the main passive tree, and the Acolyte can now also summon a companion, similar to Demon Magus. Its tooltip wasn't shown yet.
